newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products prices steady on APIs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products prices steady on APIs.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline and distillate prices were steady late Tuesday on uninspiring weekly stocks estimates released late in the day, traders said.
The weekly American Petroleum Institute survey pegged gasoline inventories 522,000 barrels below the prior week but 2.61 million barrels above the same week last year.
High sulphur diesel stocks were drawn down 121,000 barrels on the week, and low sulphur diesel inventories rose 275,000 barrels last week, the trade group said.
"This reports seems pretty neutral," one trader said.

West Coast refineries were operating at 90.5 percent of capacity, up 0.3 percentage points on the week. By comparison, refineries nationwide were operating at 93.7 percent of rated capacity, up 0.8 percentage points.

Traders said Chevron's Los Angeles-area catalytic cracker at El Segundo returned to service over the weekend, with the increased production offset by a coker fire at Mobil's Los Angeles area refinery.
Regular unleaded gasoline bids rose 0.50 cent a gallon, with discussion in Los Angeles at 62.50/63 cents a gallon.
Jet fuel made a similar upward move to 74 cents a gallon bid, 74.50 cents asked.
